range.title: Range
range.help: The preview shows the video with the widgets as they will be exported. Play or scrub it, then set where the export starts and ends: drag the handles, type times as m:ss.mmm, or press I / O at the playhead.
range.followsData: Without a start or end, the export follows the data range set in the Track step ({start} – {end}).

output.title: Output
output.videoHelp: The videos with the widgets burned in.
output.sequenceHelp: One PNG per frame with only the widgets, to composite in an editor.
output.defaultHint: Not chosen: it goes next to the videos (or the data), named after the project, without replacing an earlier export.
output.browserVideoHint: The browser asks where to save it when the export starts, or downloads it when done.
output.browserFolderHint: The browser asks for the folder when the export starts.
output.zipHint: The browser cannot write into a folder: the frames are downloaded as one zip file.

format.title: Format
format.canvasHelp: The output size is the canvas the widgets are placed on (Template step): changing its shape moves them.

encoding.title: Encoding
encoding.customHelp: Custom values, kept with the project.
encoding.accelerationHelp: Choose a graphics card to encode the video on it; the CPU takes over when it cannot encode this format.
encoding.scaling: Scaling (when the output size differs from a video)
encoding.scalingHelp: DLSS and XeSS are not offered: they are temporal upscalers that need motion vectors and depth from a game engine, which recorded video does not have. The FSR 1 style option upscales with Lanczos and sharpens with AMD's CAS, the two stages of FSR 1.
encoding.browserHelp: Encoded by this browser on the device's hardware: 8-bit SDR, with the audio re-encoded. The scaling filter, 10-bit and HDR need the desktop app.

notes.sdrConverted: YouTube converts SDR uploads to 8-bit Rec.709 limited range: a Rec.709 limited output looks the same before and after uploading.
notes.h264TenBit: 10-bit H.264 is encoded on the CPU only (GPU H.264 encoders are 8-bit) and YouTube converts it to 8-bit anyway: choose an 8-bit output or the HEVC preset.
notes.hdrNeedsHdrOutput: YouTube treats a video as HDR only with a 10-bit Rec.2020 HLG or PQ output: set the colour space and depth in Format.
notes.frameRate: The output frame rate is outside this preset's range (YouTube plays at most 60 fps): choose the preset again to convert it.
notes.socialSdr: The app plays 8-bit Rec.709 SDR video: other colour settings are converted when uploading.
notes.socialSize: The output is not this preset's format: choose the preset again to move the canvas to it.
notes.socialFrameRate: The output frame rate is outside this preset's range (the apps play at most 60 fps): choose the preset again to convert it.

encoding.estimatedSizeHelp: From the bitrate and the length of the range: the real size varies a little with the encoder and the footage.

run.title: Export
run.help: Widgets are drawn on several threads; the video is decoded and encoded on the GPU when possible. You can keep working meanwhile.
run.helpSequence: Widgets are drawn on several threads and each frame is written as a PNG file. You can keep working meanwhile.
run.preparing: Preparing: loading values, choosing the encoder…
run.doneGpu: The widgets were blended on the graphics card.
run.cancelled: Export cancelled; the unfinished file was removed.
run.cancelledSequence: Export cancelled; the frames already written were kept.
run.moving: Moving the video from the temporary folder…
run.throttled: Slowed down: the disk of the videos is busy.

waitingOn.encoder: Limited by ffmpeg: decoding, encoding or the disk.

disk.title: Disk
disk.slowHelp: For a hard drive that also holds the videos: the video is flushed to the disk regularly instead of in large bursts, and the export slows down while the disk answers slowly, so reading the videos never stalls.
disk.stageInTemp: Write to the temporary folder first
disk.stageInTempHelp: The video is written to the system's temporary folder (usually on another disk) and moved to its place once done, so the disk of the videos only reads while encoding. Needs room for the whole video there.
disk.maxSpeedHelp: Caps the encoding speed, which caps the reads and writes too: 1 encodes as fast as the video plays. Empty for no limit.
